questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: From the list of available exchange destinations on the UCPH physics website, I selected a set of very good destinations from an academic point of view. From that list, I simply chose the destination with the best weather and beaches (quite literally)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was amazing! Only drawback is that the estimated costs of living in San Diego provided by the University of California were grossly underestimated

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I recieved an abundance of information constantly before and during my stay. So finding information was easy, but important information drowned in a sea of irrelevant information. The real challenge was sorting the important information from everything else.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received support from the virtual advising center at UCSD for study planning and pre-requisite approval

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Too much irrelevant information

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I-House
General undergrad housing

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Three levels of meal plans were available (opt-out was not an option). The meal plan was way too expensive considering how much food you got from it, so most students opted for the smallest meal plan. Cooking facilities in the I-House apartments were fine, and shopping from on- and off-campus supermarkets was easy and fairly priced.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is overall a very good experience! And they should choose the smallest meal plan

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Be aware that you are basically treated as a child if you live on campus at any American university

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Pre-requisite approval (of courses taken at my home university) was overly complicated and took so long that I almost missed registration deadlines

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First you had to apply for course equivalency and prove that the courses you ha taken at your home university matches courses offered by UCSD. After obtaining equivalency decisions, you have to apply for pre-approval with the approved courses. After this, you can register for courses easily on the UCSD website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The virtual advising center was a great help. However, I wish it was possible to call or see an advisor because the communication via the advising center took very long time and was generally cumbersome.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I eventually successfully registered for all the classes I wanted, but it was a hassle practically every time

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start the course equivalency/pre-approval process as soon as possible!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Physics programme is generally very good

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took uppper devision undergraduate courses for 4th year students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: You are expected to learn mainly from lectures - not from textbooks or notes. This means that taking good notes is essential because you often cannot find the course content in writing. Also theoretical exercises at UCSD were different. At UCPH, the students work on problems at the exercises, and the TA helps the students individually and answers questions. At UCSD, the TA goes through the problems on the board as if he/she were giving a lecture.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Biological Physics
Spacecraft Guidance and Navigation
Aerodynamics
Physical Basis of Global Warming

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Quantum Physics III
SIO 199 - special studies (like a project outside course scope at UCPH)
Aerospace Engineering Lab

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Biological Physics. An amazing course with an exciting final project structured as a regular research project. Interesting topic as well, and excellent professor!
Aerodynamics. A very good introduction to a topic that we do not teach at UCPH. Very useful for geoscientific and industrial applications. Very good lecture notes
Quantum Physics III. Just a well-structured quantum physics course. Unlike many other courses, the professor in this course provides a set of extensive notes covering all of the course contents. This is good because topics in advanced quantum mechanics are not covered coherently in a single textbook, so the notes are very good for future reference as well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Mandatory health insurance even though my travel insurance includes health insurance

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food and housing were more expensive than expected. Public transportation was free for students.
Eating out (restaurants etc) and material things was cheaper than expected.
Sports facilities were free for students

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The sport and fitness options offered for free by UCSD were amazing

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I could never list all clubs, activities and societies available to students at UCSD. If you can imagine something, UCSD for sure has it. I personally took part in:
- Sunday Supper for all the international students
- Surfing events
- Dia de los Muertos
- 5km exercise run
- Member of the local rowing club, and took part in several competitions
- Surfing

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Surfing. You have to surf with a location like that!
Try some of the sport/athletic offerings from the university
Sunday supper is great
Try making a big deal out of the American an South American activities like Dia de los Muertos, St. Patrick's Day, Thanksgiving, etc

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on trips to some of the surrounding national paks and monuments
Go to the city
Chill and enjoy the beach
Use the sports facilities

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy - Americans are very welcoming

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Remember to try to meet local students. You can do this by joinging clubs, sports teams, etc. Many exchange students make the mistake of only hanging out with other exchange students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I was surprised with the division and racism in the American society. That fact that people primarily prefer to hang out with others from their own ethnic group created a division that I had never imagined. In the beginning, I found it challenging to adjust to the fact that there are certain things that I as a white man cannot do or say without appearing racist. This includes things that would be non-controversial in Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The general openness of Americans is great. They are welcoming, and they appreciate new ideas and thoughts. It is generally a very positive environment.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
You're in for a good time! Remember to get the most out of your stay by socializing with the local students and community and exploring the area and the city.
Academics are important, but remember to leave some time to have fun!
Be prepared for your stay to become more expensive than planned

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met, lived with, studied with, and rowed with made my experience great. In 20 years, I think I will mostly remember the people, the sun, the nature, and the general "California vibe".

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Signing up for courses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: My time at UCSD was awesome

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
